items.title: Jimmy Wormworth interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002
items.q: I was their second drummer. I took Walter Bolden’s place... Jon Dave and Annie didn’t overdub anything they just sang along with the band... they hired me.

ctx.x: Right. Well tell me how Lambert, Hendricks & Ross came about.

Well from what I understand, I was their second drummer. I took Walter Bolden’s place. That was after they had recorded their first Columbia album “The Hottest New Group in Jazz.” From what I understand Jon had moved to New York, Dave had lived here, I’m not sure if he was from here but he had lived here, and he wrote, I’m sure it’s fairly common knowledge that he wrote the arrangements for Charlie Parker’s “Old Folks,” the vocal arrangements and a few others. And on the record I think the vocal group is called…
Yeah, but you ended up with them after their first Columbia— © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
